items.stem: What best describes a Microsoft Loop component?

options.text: A portable piece of content that stays synced wherever it is shared
options.rationale: Correct: Loop components synchronize across apps and stay up to date.

options.text: A static screenshot of a document
options.rationale: Incorrect: a Loop component is live, not a static image.
Incorrect: Loop components work across Teams, Outlook, and more.
Incorrect: a Loop component is not a driver.

items.explanation: Correct: Loop components synchronize across apps and stay up to date.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Loop components are true? (Select TWO.)

options.text: They are stored as .loop files in OneDrive or SharePoint
options.rationale: Correct: Loop components are .loop files stored in OneDrive/SharePoint.

options.text: Recipients can edit them inline and see updates instantly
options.rationale: Correct: everyone in a chat, email, or document can edit inline.

options.text: They cannot be shared in Microsoft Teams
options.rationale: Incorrect: Loop components were first available in Teams.
Incorrect: they sync through the cloud, not offline only.

items.explanation: Correct: Loop components are .loop files stored in OneDrive/SharePoint.

items.stem: Where are Loop components created in Teams or Outlook automatically saved?

options.rationale: Correct: components created in Teams or Outlook are saved to OneDrive.
Incorrect: they are stored in the cloud, not only locally.
Incorrect: they are not published publicly by default.
Incorrect: they are saved as files, not only in drafts.

items.explanation: Correct: components created in Teams or Outlook are saved to OneDrive.
